text:
Jordan: Hey all, green on day 1. Quick environment oddities: on my M1 Mac Homebrew installed to /opt/homebrew but my cloned dotfiles assume /usr/local. I'm using fish. Also asdf installed node 18 but our tiny frontend expects 16. Any quick non-invasive fixes?

Maya: Congrats! For brew, prefer adjusting dotfiles to call `$(brew --prefix)` instead of hardcoding. For fish, add: `set -x PATH (brew --prefix)/bin $PATH` to ~/.config/fish/config.fish.

Jordan: Nice. For node 16 with asdf what's simplest?

Maya: `asdf plugin-add nodejs || true; asdf install nodejs 16.20.0; asdf local nodejs 16.20.0` in the repo dir. If nodejs plugin complains about GPG, `brew install gnupg` first.

Jordan: Gotcha. SSH: my SSH agent isn't forwarding into devcontainer so I can't push. Any standard trick?

Ops: Use the VS Code Remote setting to enable agent forwarding or mount your SSH socket into the container. For Mac, add `ForwardAgent yes` in ~/.ssh/config and in container devcontainer.json set `runArgs": ["-v","${env:SSH_AUTH_SOCK}:/ssh-agent","-e","SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/ssh-agent"]`.

Jordan: Sweet. Where should I stash local dev secrets? .envrc or 1Password?

DevEx: 1Password is canonical; keep only non-sensitive samples in repo. We add `op` commands into .envrc to pull secrets: e.g., `export API_KEY=$(op item get "redwood/dev-api" --fields label=password)`. direnv then protects loading.

Jordan: Who owns the dotfiles repo? I can send a tiny PR to replace /usr/local with brew prefix.

Maya: Ping @Ops or open PR to dotfiles/redwood-dotfiles; mention fish compatibility. Happy to review.

infra-bot: Onboarding note: updated handbook entry for Apple Silicon brew paths and asdf GPG prerequisites. https://go.redwood/handbook/onboarding/setup

Jordan: Thanks everyone, that unblocked me. Will open the PR and update my dotfiles fork.
